tier_reason: Upgraded B to A: Aras Pranckevicius's public harness (aras-p/test_exr_htj2k_jxl src/main.cpp, src/image_mop.cpp, src/image_exr.cpp) writes exact per-codec ratio and GB/s numbers to checked-in result files (img/win-ryzen5950x-20250908.html, img/mac-m4max-20250908.html) that print the CPU model and thread count; the README names the compilers (Visual Studio 2022 v17.14, Xcode clang 16) and the CMake Release config from CMakePresets.json/CMakeLists.txt fixes the flags, and the 10 test files are publicly downloadable. The run is independent of the meshoptimizer author.

corrections.baseline: OpenEXR 3.4.0 ZIP compression at level 4 (deflate through OpenEXR's bundled libdeflate, OPENEXR_FORCE_INTERNAL_DEFLATE ON); the same harness also runs EXR RLE, PIZ, HTJ2K_32/HTJ2K_256 (OpenJPH inside OpenEXR) and libjxl lossless at efforts 1/3/4/7/8. No standalone zstd, fpzip or zfp baseline in this harness.
corrections.claimed_speedup: From img/win-ryzen5950x-20250908.html (Ryzen 9 5950X, 16 threads, 10 files 3122.4 MB, best of 3 runs): meshoptimizer vertex codec level 2 (Mop2) ratio 2.011 at 1.600 GB/s compress and 7.861 GB/s decompress versus EXR ZIP level 4 ratio 1.873 at 1.172 GB/s compress and 2.526 GB/s decompress, i.e. about 1.37x compression and 3.1x decompression throughput at a 7% better ratio (derived from page data). Mop1: 2.004 GB/s compress (1.71x, derived) and 8.016 GB/s decompress at ratio 1.966. Mop2 plus zstd level 1: ratio 2.248, 1.533 GB/s compress, 6.739 GB/s decompress. EXR HTJ2K_256: ratio 1.947, 0.709/1.045 GB/s; libjxl effort 7: ratio 2.180, 0.050/0.382 GB/s. On Apple M4 Max (img/mac-m4max-20250908.html): Mop2 3.104 GB/s compress and 14.808 GB/s decompress versus ZIP4 1.723 and 5.993 GB/s (1.80x and 2.47x, derived from page data). README conclusion: mesh optimizer is 'very far ahead of others towards top right of the chart'.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMake Release config (CMakePresets.json x64-release, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release; no extra flags in CMakeLists.txt, so CMake's Release defaults apply: /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG for MSVC, -O3 -DNDEBUG for clang), C++17, static libs; Visual Studio 2022 v17.14 on Windows, Xcode clang 16 on Mac; OpenEXR 3.4.0, libjxl main pre-v0.12 (029cec4), meshoptimizer v0.25, zstd 1.5.7, all via FetchContent
corrections.hardware: Windows: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor, 16 threads; Mac: Apple M4 Max, 16 threads
corrections.workload: Lossless round trip of 10 floating-point EXR images (3122.4 MB raw; RGB/RGBA half and float, multi-layer renders with up to 37 channels, two Poly Haven HDRIs) into and out of an in-memory stream. The meshoptimizer path ('Mop') splits pixels into 16K-pixel chunks, encodes each with meshopt_encodeVertexBufferLevel (vertex codec, levels 0-3, encoding version 1; pixels treated as vertices padded to a multiple of 4 bytes; no meshopt filters), optionally followed by a zstd pass (levels 1/3/10/20), chunks run in parallel on 16 threads; OpenEXR uses setGlobalThreadCount(16). Save and load times include container writing; every codec's output is checked bit-exact with CompareImages; best of 3 runs.
corrections.caveats: Off-label use: 'MOP' is not an image format but meshoptimizer's mesh vertex-buffer codec repurposed by the benchmark author to pack pixel chunks into a custom container with no interop, while the EXR baselines write standard OpenEXR files; both sides are lossless and both are multithreaded, but meshoptimizer offers no image API, so this is the vertex codec's general byte-delta/bit-packing scheme, not a supported image feature. The README's embedded charts are the 2025-06-30 PNGs; the exact numbers above come from the 2025-09-08 HTML result files, which match the library versions the README lists. fp16 subnormals are flushed to zero in the input before all codecs (for libjxl's sake), so 'lossless' applies to the sanitized data. Test images are mostly path-traced renders with noise; the author notes natural images may behave differently. The float-compression series in aras-p/float_compr_tester (meshoptimizer v0.18 versus zstd, lz4, fpzip, zfp and others) is a different harness whose results are only in blocked blog posts. meshoptimizer's own purpose is mesh optimization; it may belong in another category.

notes: Exact numbers found in checked-in HTML result files, so chart reading is no longer needed; upgraded to A. Codec is the vertex codec only (no filters), optionally stacked with zstd; baselines are OpenEXR ZIP/PIZ/RLE/HTJ2K and libjxl, not fpzip/zfp/zstd. zeux/meshoptimizer appears nowhere else in data/, so not a duplicate.

tier_reason: Independent third-party measurement with public code (dicom-codecs tests/main.cpp and tests/benchmark.cpp, wrappers lib/openjph/encoder.cpp and src/openjpeg/encoder.cpp) and a stated machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro), but no compiler is named and each case is one timed iteration after one warm-up, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: dicom-codecs README (MacBook Pro M1 Pro), lossless decode time per image: OpenJPH 4.09 ms versus OpenJPEG 24.73 ms (8-bit color US 640x480), 1.43 versus 15.65 ms (12-bit gray MR 512x512), 1.53 versus 22.27 ms (16-bit gray CT 512x512), 89.20 versus 1447.63 ms (12-bit gray MG 3064x4664): about 6.0x, 10.9x, 14.6x and 16.2x (derived from page data). OpenJPH also beats CharLS JPEG-LS lossless (7.46, 3.14, 3.46, 212.92 ms; about 1.8x to 2.4x, derived) but Kakadu is faster still (1.13, 0.51, 0.64, 29.36 ms). Encode times are measured by the harness but not published in the README.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: build.sh: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release, on arm64 also -DOJPH_DISABLE_INTEL_SIMD=ON; OpenJPEG compiled from source with -ffast-math in Release and threading stubbed out (MUTEX_stub); compiler not stated. Submodules pinned at OpenJPH 5aab43f and OpenJPEG 41c25e3 (updated 2023-12-14)
corrections.workload: dicom-codecs tests/main.cpp: each codec encodes the raw test image from dicom-codecs/test-data (US1-640-480-3-8-0, MR4-512-512-1-12-0, CT1-512-512-1-16-1, MG1-3064-4664-1-12-0) with its own encoder, then the timed loop decodes its own codestream once after one warm-up decode (iterations = 1). OpenJPH writes an HTJ2K (Part 15) codestream, reversible, RPCL, 64x64 code blocks, decomposition count chosen so the lowest level is at most 64 px (3 for US/MR/CT, 6 for MG), no colour transform; OpenJPEG writes a JPEG 2000 Part 1 J2K codestream, reversible, RPCL, 64x64 blocks, 5 decompositions, RCT on the colour image. Both are single-threaded and lossless; round trips are checked before timing.
corrections.caveats: The two libraries decode different codestreams: OpenJPH decodes HTJ2K (Part 15 block coder) while OpenJPEG decodes JPEG 2000 Part 1 (EBCOT/MQ coder), so most of the gap is the HT format rather than the library; OpenJPEG at the pinned commit also contains an HTJ2K decoder (ht_dec.c) but it was not timed on OpenJPH's stream. Settings differ slightly (decomposition levels 3 versus 5 on three images, RCT only for OpenJPEG on the colour image). Compressed sizes are not reported (the ratio printout is commented out), so the speed versus size trade-off is unknown. One iteration per case, compiler unstated, OpenJPH built with Intel SIMD disabled on arm64, OpenJPEG built single-threaded with -ffast-math. The dicom-codecs repository calls itself WIP (10 stars, last commit 2023-12-14). The libjpeg-turbo8 row (4.06 ms on the US image) is lossy baseline JPEG and not comparable. The OpenJPH README publishes no numbers of its own.

notes: Baseline is OpenJPEG (JPEG 2000 Part 1, lossless); Kakadu (proprietary) and CharLS (JPEG-LS) are also in the same run. Lossless settings match (both reversible), lossy settings were not benchmarked. Kept at B as an independent measurement with public code; the format-versus-library caveat is spelled out.

tier_reason: First-party PSNR-versus-time chart (doc/kodim-chart.png) with an unlabeled time axis and no machine or compiler; the repo's harness icbc_test.cpp times only ICBC, and doc/results.txt lists ICBC-only timings per CPU and compiler with no baseline rows, so the baseline numbers cannot be traced to public code.

corrections.baseline: RGBCX 1.12 (levels 0-18), squish 1.15, stb_dxt 1.09 with improvements proposed by Rich Geldreich and Ignacio Castano (not stock), and AMD CMP_Core V4.0.4855
corrections.claimed_speedup: Chart only (doc/kodim-chart.png, average PSNR on Kodim+Waterloo versus encode time, time unit unlabeled; readings approximate): at the top quality point (PSNR about 30.9) ICBC-AVX512 takes about 5.5 versus about 20.6 for RGBCX and about 19.3 for ICBC-Scalar (about 3.7x versus RGBCX, derived from chart reading); near PSNR 30.83-30.84 ICBC-AVX512 is about 1.1 versus about 5.1 for RGBCX. squish sits at about 7.4 for PSNR about 30.43 and AMD CMP at about 14.6 for PSNR about 30.25, both above the ICBC-AVX512 curve (under 1.0 at those PSNRs). stb_dxt tops out near PSNR 30.06 at about 0.3, where ICBC and RGBCX are similar. ICBC-Scalar is slower than RGBCX at almost every quality level, so the lead comes from SIMD (AVX-512 in the chart).
corrections.caveats: The result is a first-party PSNR-versus-time chart with no hardware, compiler or time unit; the AVX-512 series implies an AVX-512 CPU but the machine is not named. doc/results.txt holds ICBC-only timings (Sky Lake AVX512, Coffee Lake, Ryzen Threadripper 2990WX, Apple M1 Pro, Raspberry Pi, etc.) with no baseline rows, and icbc_test.cpp (multithreaded through ic_pfor) runs only ICBC, so how the baselines were timed (threading, flags) is unknown. The comparison pits ICBC's AVX-512 path against scalar RGBCX; ICBC-Scalar is slower than RGBCX across most of the range. stb_dxt was a modified 1.09, not the stock release. The README itself says RGBCX is most likely a better choice for a well supported, actively developed library, and RGBCX is already catalogued. Texture-encoder baselines (stb_dxt, rgbcx, squish, nvtt) are outside the category's baseline list. Last commit 2022-11-09.

notes: No table of baseline numbers exists in the repo; doc/results.txt is ICBC-only. Chart readings in the record match the image. NVTT is not a separate baseline here (ICBC is NVTT's BC1 encoder). Rich Geldreich's BC1 benchmark posts (richg42.blogspot.com) compare stb_dxt 1.09, icbc and rgbcx 1.12 but blogs are blocked, so not used.
